title: Control radiation geometry of a normalized projected excitation without equating it to a gate
statement: If fixed P has uniform projection residual delta<1, v(q)=Pu(q)/||Pu(q)|| is well defined with c_min=sqrt(1-delta^2). For the supplied ideal angular distribution p(mu)=3*(1+mu^2)/8, L(q,theta)=sqrt(v*G_theta*v) obeys |Delta L|<=sqrt(N)*L_N*(2*|Delta q|/c_min+sqrt(2/5)*|Delta theta|), L_N=sqrt((N^2-1)/12). This is a geometry/variation tool, not full scattering fidelity.

requires: Fixed P, supplied uniform delta<1 and centered phase convention; declared ideal perpendicular electric-dipole angular bath.

body: Use centered site coordinates in both phase vectors and angular maps; their scalar rephasings leave the Gram norm invariant. Normalized projections differ by at most2*L_N*|Delta q|/c_min. The angular map has norm<=sqrt(N); its theta derivative has norm<=sqrt(N)*L_N*sqrt(integral p*mu^2), with integral p=1 and integral p*mu^2=2/5. Triangle inequality yields the stated bound. For validated monotone phase grids, add the maximum adjacent phase-step allowance to max_grid L. The exact ideal angular characteristic is g(x)=3/2*(sin(x)/x+cos(x)/x^2-sin(x)/x^3),g(0)=1. Given a validated upper L_max, the source intensity ratio obeys lambda<=rho_max*L_max^2/(N*c_min^2). The isolated-scalar resonance error2*sqrt(lambda/(1+lambda)) requires that separate hypothetical response interface; an array has not been shown to realize it. Quoted sub-percent tables use unacquired floating eigensystems/trigonometric data, not available outward intervals.
